q: A student scores 72 out of 90. What is the percentage?
The price of sugar rises by 25%. By what percent must a family cut its use so that the spending stays the same?
why: New use is 1/1.25 = 0.8 of the old, a cut of 20%.

q: A town's population of 50,000 grows by 10% a year. What is it after 2 years?
What is 15% of 15% of 2,000?
In an exam 35% failed in Maths, 25% in English and 10% in both. What percent passed in both?
why: Failed in at least one: 35 + 25 − 10 = 50%. So 50% passed in both.

q: A's salary is 25% more than B's. By what percent is B's salary less than A's?
why: If B = 100, A = 125. The difference 25 is 20% of 125.

q: After spending 80% of his income, a man saves ₹6,000. What is his income?
why: ₹6,000 is the 20% he saves, so the income is 6,000 ÷ 0.2 = 30,000.

q: A phone bought for ₹12,000 is sold for ₹10,800. What is the loss percent?
why: The loss is 1,200, which is 10% of 12,000.

q: By selling 12 pens for ₹100 a shop loses 20%. How many pens should it sell for ₹100 to gain 20%?
why: At a 20% loss, 12 pens cost 100/0.8 = 125, so one costs 125/12. To gain 20% the price per pen is 1.2 × 125/12 = 12.5, and ₹100 buys 8.

q: The cost price of 20 items equals the selling price of 16 items. What is the profit percent?
why: If each costs ₹1, 16 items sell for ₹20: a profit of 4 on 16, which is 25%.

q: Two articles are sold for ₹990 each, one at a 10% profit and the other at a 10% loss. The overall result is:
why: Selling two things at the same price with equal profit and loss percent always gives a loss of (10)²/100 = 1%.

q: A trader marks goods 40% above cost and gives a 20% discount. His profit percent is:
A shopkeeper gains ₹150 by selling a fan for ₹1,650. What is his profit percent?
Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% are the same as a single discount of:
why: 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.72, so the price falls by 28%.

q: A bag marked ₹1,200 is sold for ₹960. What is the discount percent?
why: The discount is 240, which is 20% of 1,200.

q: What sum gives ₹900 as simple interest in 3 years at 6% a year?
A sum becomes ₹7,200 in 3 years and ₹8,400 in 5 years at simple interest. What is the sum?
why: Two years of interest is 1,200, so one year is 600. Three years is 1,800, and 7,200 − 1,800 = 5,400.

q: ₹8,000 at 5% a year, compounded yearly, for 3 years gives an amount of:
A sum doubles in 5 years at compound interest. In how many years will it become 8 times?
why: 8 = 2³, so it needs three doublings: 3 × 5 = 15 years.

q: The compound interest on ₹10,000 for 2 years at 10% a year, compounded every six months, is:
why: Half-yearly the rate is 5% for 4 periods: 10,000 × 1.05⁴ − 10,000 = 2,155.06.

q: A and B together finish a job in 8 days. A alone takes 12 days. How long does B alone take?
why: B's daily work is 1/8 − 1/12 = 1/24, so B takes 24 days.

q: A can do a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. They work together for 3 days, then A leaves. How many more days does B need?
why: In 3 days they finish 3 × (1/10 + 1/15) = 1/2. B does the other half at 1/15 a day: 7.5 days.

q: 12 men can finish a job in 10 days. After 4 days, 4 men leave. How many days does the rest of the work take?
why: The job is 120 man-days. After 4 days 72 are left, and 8 men need 72 ÷ 8 = 9 days.

q: If 6 people can paint a house in 8 days, how many people are needed to paint it in 4 days?
why: 6 × 8 = 48 person-days, and 48 ÷ 4 = 12.

q: Pipe A fills a tank in 4 hours and pipe B in 6 hours. Together they fill it in:
Two pipes fill a tank in 10 and 15 minutes, and a third empties it in 20 minutes. With all three open, the tank fills in:
A cyclist covers 36 km in 2 hours 15 minutes. His speed is:
why: 2 hours 15 minutes is 2.25 hours, and 36 ÷ 2.25 = 16.

q: A train running at 72 km/h crosses a 300 m platform in 30 seconds. How long is the train?
why: 72 km/h is 20 m/s. In 30 s it covers 600 m: the platform plus the train, so the train is 300 m.

q: Walking at 3/4 of his usual speed, a man is 20 minutes late. His usual time is:
why: At 3/4 the speed the time is 4/3 of usual. The extra 1/3 is 20 minutes, so the usual time is 60.

q: Two trains start at the same time from cities 300 km apart and move towards each other at 60 km/h and 40 km/h. They meet after:
why: They close the gap at 100 km/h: 300 ÷ 100 = 3 hours.

q: A boat's speed in still water is 10 km/h and the stream flows at 2 km/h. How long does a 24 km trip upstream take?
why: Upstream the speed is 10 − 2 = 8 km/h, and 24 ÷ 8 = 3 hours.

q: A thief runs at 8 km/h. A policeman starts 10 minutes later at 10 km/h. How long after starting does he catch the thief?
why: In 10 minutes the thief is 8/6 km ahead. The policeman gains 2 km/h, so he needs (4/3) ÷ 2 h = 40 minutes.

q: If 3 : x = 12 : 20, then x is:
The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3 : 2. If there are 12 girls, how many students are there?
why: 12 girls are 2 parts, so one part is 6. The class has 5 parts: 30.

q: Incomes of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 4 and their spending in the ratio 3 : 2. If each saves ₹2,000, A's income is:
A puts ₹40,000 into a business for 12 months and B puts ₹60,000 for 6 months. Out of a profit of ₹14,000, A gets:
why: Shares go by money × time: 480,000 : 360,000 = 4 : 3. A gets 4/7 of 14,000 = 8,000.

q: A, B and C start a business with ₹20,000, ₹30,000 and ₹50,000. After a year, C's share of the profit is ₹15,000. The total profit is:
why: C's money is half the total, so C gets half the profit. The total is 30,000.

q: The average of 11 results is 50. The first six average 49 and the last six average 52. The sixth result is:
why: 6 × 49 + 6 × 52 − 11 × 50 = 294 + 312 − 550 = 56. The sixth result was counted twice.

q: A batsman's average after 16 innings is 40. What must he score in the 17th innings to raise his average to 42?
why: He needs 17 × 42 = 714 in all, and has 640: he needs 74.

q: The average of 4, 8, 15, 16, 23 and 42 is:
why: The sum is 108, and 108 ÷ 6 = 18.

q: In what ratio must rice at ₹40/kg be mixed with rice at ₹55/kg to get a mixture worth ₹45/kg?
A 40-litre can has milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much of the mixture must be replaced with water so the ratio becomes 1 : 1?
why: Milk must fall from 30 to 20 litres, so 1/3 of the mixture is replaced: 40/3 ≈ 13.33 litres.

q: The ratio of A's and B's ages is 4 : 5. After 6 years it will be 5 : 6. A's age now is:
A mother is 3 times as old as her daughter. 15 years from now she will be twice as old. How old is the daughter now?
The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 78. The largest is:
why: They are n − 2, n, n + 2 with 3n = 78, so n = 26 and the largest is 28.

q: How many numbers between 1 and 100 (inclusive) are divisible by 3 or 5?
What is the remainder when 2¹⁰ is divided by 7?
why: 2³ = 8 leaves 1, so 2⁹ leaves 1 and 2¹⁰ leaves 2.

q: How many zeros does 50! (50 factorial) end with?
why: Count the 5s: 50/5 = 10 plus 50/25 = 2, so 12.

q: What is the unit digit of 3²⁰²⁶?
why: Powers of 3 end in 3, 9, 7, 1 in turn. 2026 leaves 2 when divided by 4, so it ends in 9.

q: Which of these is a prime number?
why: 91 = 7 × 13, 87 = 3 × 29 and 93 = 3 × 31. 97 has no factor other than 1 and itself.

q: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 360. If one number is 72, the other is:
why: HCF × LCM = product: 12 × 360 ÷ 72 = 60.

q: Three bells ring every 6, 8 and 12 minutes. They ring together at 9:00. When will they next ring together?
why: The LCM of 6, 8 and 12 is 24 minutes, so 9:24.

q: What is 25% of 480 plus 40% of 250?
√(1764) equals:
If x + 1/x = 5, then x² + 1/x² is:
why: Squaring: x² + 2 + 1/x² = 25, so x² + 1/x² = 23.

q: If 2x + 3y = 12 and x − y = 1, then x is:
why: From x = y + 1: 2y + 2 + 3y = 12, so y = 2 and x = 3.

q: The roots of x² − 7x + 12 = 0 are:
The area of a rectangle 12 m long and 8 m wide is:
A circle has a circumference of 44 cm (take π = 22/7). Its area is:
why: 2πr = 44 gives r = 7, and πr² = 22/7 × 49 = 154.

q: If each side of a square grows by 20%, its area grows by:
why: 1.2² = 1.44, a 44% increase.

q: The sides of a right triangle are 6 cm and 8 cm. The hypotenuse is:
How many diagonals does a hexagon have?
The volume of a cube is 512 cm³. Its total surface area is:
why: The side is 8 cm, and 6 × 64 = 384.

q: A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm (π = 22/7). Its volume is:
In how many ways can the letters of LEVEL be arranged?
why: 5! ÷ (2! × 2!) = 120 ÷ 4 = 30, because L and E each appear twice.

q: How many 4-digit numbers can be made from 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 without repeating a digit?
why: The first digit cannot be 0: 4 choices, then 4, 3 and 2: 4 × 4 × 3 × 2 = 96.

q: In how many ways can 3 students be picked from 8 for a project?
A team of 3 men and 2 women is chosen from 5 men and 4 women. In how many ways?
Two dice are thrown. The probability that the total is 7 is:
why: 6 of the 36 outcomes add to 7: 1/6.

q: Two cards are drawn without putting back from a pack of 52. The probability that both are aces is:
A number is picked from 1 to 20. The probability that it is a multiple of 3 or 4 is:
why: Multiples of 3: 6, of 4: 5, of both (12): 1. That is 10 numbers out of 20.

q: 15 August 2026 is a Saturday. What day is 15 August 2027?
why: The year between has no 29 February, so it is 365 days: one extra day, Sunday.

q: At what time between 2 and 3 o'clock are the hands of a clock together?
why: The minute hand gains 5.5° a minute and starts 60° behind: 60 ÷ 5.5 = 10 10/11 minutes past 2.

q: How many times do the hands of a clock coincide in a day?
why: They meet 11 times every 12 hours, so 22 times a day.

q: A company's sales were ₹40 lakh, ₹50 lakh and ₹65 lakh in three years. The growth from the second to the third year was:
Out of 400 students, 30% chose Physics, 25% Chemistry and the rest Biology. How many chose Biology?
why: Biology is 45% of 400 = 180.

q: A pie chart shows rent as 90° of a monthly spend of ₹48,000. How much is rent?
why: 90° is a quarter of the circle: 48,000 ÷ 4 = 12,000.

q: Find the next number: 7, 10, 16, 25, 37, ?
why: The gaps 3, 6, 9, 12 grow by 3, so the next gap is 15: 52.

q: Find the next number: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, ?
why: These are the prime numbers, and the next prime after 13 is 17.

q: Find the next number: 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ?
why: Each number is multiplied by 2, 3, 4, 5 and then 6: 120 × 6 = 720.

q: Find the missing number: 4, 9, 19, 39, ?, 159
why: Each term is double the one before, plus 1: 39 × 2 + 1 = 79.

q: A boat goes 30 km downstream in 2 hours and 18 km upstream in 2 hours. The speed of the boat in still water is:
why: Downstream 15 km/h and upstream 9 km/h. The boat's own speed is the average: 12 km/h.

q: At 10% simple interest, how much interest does ₹2,500 earn in 2 years?
A number is first increased by 10% and then by another 10%. The total increase is:
A dishonest shopkeeper sells at cost price but uses a 900 g weight for 1 kg. His gain percent is:
why: He gives 900 g for the price of 1,000 g: a gain of 100/900 ≈ 11.11%.

q: A is twice as fast as B. Together they finish a job in 12 days. How long would A alone take?
why: If B does 1 unit a day, A does 2: together 3 units a day for 12 days = 36 units. A alone takes 36 ÷ 2 = 18 days.

q: How far does a car travel in 45 minutes at 80 km/h?
why: 45 minutes is 0.75 hours, and 80 × 0.75 = 60.

q: The average weight of 8 people rises by 2.5 kg when one of them, who weighs 65 kg, is replaced. The new person weighs:
why: The total rises by 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg, so the new person weighs 65 + 20 = 85 kg.

q: If MANGO is written as NBOHP, how is APPLE written?
why: Every letter moves one place forward: A→B, P→Q, P→Q, L→M, E→F.

q: If TABLE is coded as 20-1-2-12-5, how is CHAIR coded?
why: Each letter is its place in the alphabet: C3 H8 A1 I9 R18.

q: In a code, ROAD is written as URDG. How is SWAN written?
why: Each letter moves three places forward: S→V, W→Z, A→D, N→Q.

q: If FRIEND is written as HUMJTK, how is CANDLE written?
why: The letters move forward by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 places: C+2=E, A+3=D, N+4=R, D+5=I, L+6=R, E+7=L.

q: Rahul's mother is the only daughter of Sita's father. How is Sita related to Rahul?
why: The only daughter of Sita's father is Sita herself, so Sita is Rahul's mother.

q: A is the brother of B. B is the daughter of C. D is the father of A. How is C related to D?
why: A and B are brother and sister, so D, A's father, is B's father too. C is B's other parent, so C is D's wife.

q: Pointing to a man, a woman says, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?
why: The only daughter of her mother is the woman herself, so she is his mother.

q: A man walks 10 m south, turns left and walks 10 m, then turns left and walks 10 m. Which direction is he from his start?
why: South, then left (east), then left (north) back up: he ends 10 m east of the start.

q: At 6 in the morning a man stands facing the sun. His shadow falls to his:
why: The morning sun is in the east. Facing it, his shadow falls behind him.

q: Riya walks 4 km east, then 3 km north. How far is she from where she started?
why: The straight-line distance is √(4² + 3²) = 5 km.

q: Five friends sit in a row. A is to the left of B, C is to the right of B, D is between A and B, and E is at the far right. Who sits in the middle?
why: The order is A, D, B, C, E, so B is in the middle.

q: Five people sit in a row facing north. P sits at one end, Q sits next to P, R sits in the middle and S is not next to R. Where does T sit?
why: With P at seat 1, Q is at 2 and R at 3. S cannot be at 2 or 4, so S is at 5 and T at 4, between R and S. Starting P at the other end gives the mirror image, with the same answer.

q: In a queue, Aman is 8th from the front and 13th from the back. How many people are in the queue?
why: 8 + 13 − 1 = 20, since Aman is counted twice.

q: In a class of 40, Neha is 15th from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?
Doctor is to Hospital as Teacher is to:
why: A doctor works in a hospital; a teacher works in a school.

q: Cup is to Coffee as Bowl is to:
why: A cup holds coffee; a bowl holds soup.

q: Find the pair that is related the same way as Bird : Nest
why: A nest is the home a bird lives in; a kennel is the home a dog lives in.

q: Which is the odd one out?
why: Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets; the Moon is a satellite.

q: Which number does not belong: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, 50, 64
why: The numbers are n² + 1 (1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49 plus one). The next would be 65, not 64.

q: Statements: All pens are books. All books are tables. Conclusion I: All pens are tables. Conclusion II: Some tables are pens.
why: Every pen is a book and every book a table, so all pens are tables, and therefore some tables are pens.

q: Statements: Some cats are dogs. No dog is a rat. Conclusion I: Some cats are not rats. Conclusion II: No cat is a rat.
why: The cats that are dogs cannot be rats, so some cats are not rats. Other cats might be rats, so II does not follow.

q: Statements: No student is lazy. Some lazy people are rich. Conclusion: Some rich people are not students.
options: Follows only if all rich people are lazy
why: The rich people who are lazy cannot be students, so some rich people are not students.

q: Statement: 'Use our app to book a train ticket in 2 minutes.' Which is assumed?
options: People want to book tickets quickly
why: The advert only works if people care about booking quickly.

q: Statement I: Many students failed the exam. Statement II: The exam was much harder than earlier ones. Which is most likely?
options: I is the cause, II the effect
II is the cause, I the effect
Both are effects of a third cause
why: A harder exam explains more failures, not the other way round.

q: A clock gains 5 minutes every hour. It is set right at 8 am. What time does it show at 2 pm the same day?
why: Six hours pass, and it gains 6 × 5 = 30 minutes: it shows 2:30 pm.

q: If tomorrow is Thursday, what day was it 3 days before yesterday?
why: Today is Wednesday, yesterday was Tuesday, and three days before that was Saturday.

q: A, B, C, D and E have different heights. B is taller than D but shorter than A. C is taller than A. E is the shortest. Who is the tallest?
why: The order from the top is C, A, B, D, E.

q: x is a whole number. Is x even? (1) 3x is even. (2) x + 2 is even. Which is enough?
why: If 3x is even, x must be even (for whole numbers). If x + 2 is even, x is even. Either one is enough.

q: In a group of 50, 30 like tea, 25 like coffee and 10 like both. How many like neither?
why: At least one: 30 + 25 − 10 = 45, so 5 like neither.

q: Find the next letters: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
why: The first letter moves forward and the second backward: E and V.

q: Find the next: B, E, H, K, ?
why: Each letter is three places after the last: K + 3 = N.

q: A clock shows 3:15. What time does its mirror image show?
why: The mirror time is 11:60 − 3:15 = 8:45.

q: A cube painted on all sides is cut into 27 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two painted faces?
why: Edge cubes (not corners) have two painted faces: 12 edges × 1 = 12.

q: In the same 27-cube cut, how many small cubes have no paint at all?
why: Only the one cube in the very centre is unpainted.

q: If A > B, B ≥ C and C > D, which must be true?
why: A > B ≥ C > D, so A is greater than D.

q: Which year has the same calendar as 2026?
why: Day shifts from 2026: 2027 +1, 2028 (leap) +2, 2029 +1, 2030 +1, 2031 +1, 2032 (leap) +2, 2033 +1, 2034 +1, 2035 +1, 2036 (leap) +2. That totals 14 by 2037, a whole number of weeks, and 2037 is not a leap year like 2026.

q: Which word does not belong?
why: Keyboard, mouse and scanner put data into a computer; a monitor shows output.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to ABUNDANT.
why: Abundant means existing in large amounts: plentiful.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to METICULOUS.
why: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to CANDID.
why: A candid remark is open and honest: frank.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to OBSOLETE.
why: Obsolete means no longer in use.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to EXPAND.
why: To contract is to become smaller, the opposite of expand.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to TRANSPARENT.
why: Opaque things do not let light through.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to FRUGAL.
why: Frugal means careful with money; wasteful is the opposite.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to BENEVOLENT.
why: Benevolent means kind and well-meaning; malicious means wanting to harm.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Each of the students have a laptop.
Each of the students has a laptop.
Each of the student has a laptop.
Each of the students having a laptop.
why: 'Each' is singular, so it takes 'has'.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He is more senior than me.
why: 'Senior', 'junior', 'superior' and 'inferior' take 'to', not 'than'.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have been working here since five years.
I am working here for five years.
I have been working here for five years.
I work here since five years.
why: Use 'for' with a length of time and the present perfect continuous for something still going on.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Neither the manager nor the employees was present.
Neither the manager nor the employees were present.
Neither the manager or the employees were present.
Neither the manager nor the employees is present.
why: With 'neither… nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject: 'employees were'.

q: She is good ___ mathematics.
why: We say 'good at' a subject or skill.

q: The meeting was ___ because the manager was ill.
why: 'Called off' means cancelled.

q: If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.
why: Imagined situations use 'were' for every subject: 'If I were you'.

q: Hardly had the train left ___ it started raining.
why: 'Hardly… when' (and 'no sooner… than') is the fixed pair.

q: What does 'to burn the midnight oil' mean?
options: To study or work late at night
why: It means working late into the night.

q: What does 'a blessing in disguise' mean?
options: Something bad that turns out good
why: It is a misfortune that ends up having a good result.

q: What does 'to beat around the bush' mean?
why: It means talking around a topic instead of saying it directly.

q: A person who can speak many languages is a:
why: A polyglot knows and uses several languages.

q: A government by the people is a:
why: Democracy is rule by the people.

q: Something that cannot be read because the writing is unclear is:
why: Illegible means not clear enough to be read.

q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
why: Accommodation has double c and double m.

q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
why: Occurrence has double c, double r and ends in -ence.

q: "The new metro line cut the average commute from 70 to 40 minutes, but ticket prices rose by 20%." Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Commuters save time but may pay more
why: Time went down and prices went up; nothing is said about usage.

q: "Most students who practised daily scored above 70%." Which is a fair reading?
options: Daily practice is linked to higher scores
Students who did not practise failed
why: 'Most' shows a link, not a guarantee, and says nothing about the others.

q: Arrange: (P) Then add the rice. (Q) First, boil the water. (R) Finally, drain and serve. (S) Cook it for 15 minutes.
why: Boil water, add rice, cook it, then drain and serve.

q: Change to passive: 'The committee approved the plan.'
options: The plan was approved by the committee.
The plan is approved by the committee.
The committee was approved by the plan.
The plan had approved the committee.
why: Simple past active becomes 'was + past participle' in the passive.

q: She said, 'I am tired.' In indirect speech:
options: She said that she is tired.
She said that she was tired.
She said that I was tired.
She says that she was tired.
why: After a past reporting verb, 'am' changes to 'was' and 'I' to 'she'.

q: He is ___ honest man.
why: 'Honest' starts with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so 'an'.

q: Which data structure works on Last In, First Out?
why: A stack removes the item added most recently.

q: Which structure is best for checking whether brackets in an expression are balanced?
why: Push each opening bracket and pop when its closing bracket comes; a stack matches the most recent open bracket.

q: What is the time to look up a key in a hash table on average?
why: A good hash spreads keys evenly, so a lookup checks only a few slots on average.

q: In a min-heap, where is the smallest element?
why: Every parent is no larger than its children, so the root holds the minimum.

q: What is the worst-case time to search a binary search tree with n nodes?
why: If keys arrive in sorted order the tree becomes a chain, and a search may visit all n nodes.

q: A queue is built from a circular array of size 5 holding 5 items. What happens on one more insert?
why: A fixed circular array has no free slot left, so the insert fails as an overflow.

q: How many edges does a tree with 20 nodes have?
why: A tree with n nodes always has n − 1 edges.

q: Which algorithm finds the shortest path from one vertex when all edge weights are non-negative?
why: Dijkstra's algorithm handles non-negative weights; Kruskal and Prim build spanning trees.

q: Breadth-first search uses which data structure?
why: BFS visits vertices level by level by taking them from a queue.

q: Which algorithm can detect a negative-weight cycle?
why: Bellman-Ford relaxes edges V − 1 times; if one more pass still improves a distance, there is a negative cycle.

q: Which sort has O(n log n) time in the worst case?
why: Merge sort always splits in half and merges in linear time; quick sort can fall to O(n²).

q: Which sort is usually fastest on an array that is already nearly sorted?
why: Insertion sort does little work when each item is close to its place: close to O(n).

q: Which of these sorts is stable?
why: Merge sort keeps equal keys in their original order; the others can swap them.

q: Binary search needs the array to be:
why: Binary search discards half the range by comparing with the middle, which only works on sorted data.

q: At most how many comparisons does binary search need on 1,000 sorted items?
why: 2¹⁰ = 1024 ≥ 1000, so about 10 halvings are enough.

q: What is the time complexity of two nested loops that each run n times?
why: The inner loop runs n times for each of the n outer passes: n × n.

q: What is the time complexity of this loop? i = 1; while i < n: i = i * 2
why: i doubles each time, so the loop runs about log₂ n times.

q: The recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n solves to:
why: This is merge sort's recurrence: log n levels each doing n work.

q: Which problem is usually solved with dynamic programming?
options: Finding the maximum of an array
why: 0/1 knapsack has overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure, the two signs of DP.

q: Which problem is solved correctly by a greedy method?
why: In fractional knapsack, taking the best value-per-weight item first is always optimal.

q: Which of these is not an operating system?
why: Oracle Database is a database management system that runs on an operating system.

q: What is a process?
options: A thread of the kernel only
why: A process is a running program with its own memory and state.

q: Threads of the same process share:
why: Each thread has its own stack, registers and program counter, but they share the process's memory.

q: Which scheduling algorithm can cause starvation?
why: Long jobs may wait forever if short jobs keep arriving.

q: Three jobs with burst times 6, 2 and 4 arrive together. Under shortest job first, what is the average waiting time?
why: Order 2, 4, 6: waits are 0, 2 and 6, which average 8/3 ≈ 2.67.

q: Which is not one of the four conditions needed for deadlock?
why: The condition is no preemption; allowing preemption breaks deadlock.

q: Thrashing happens when:
options: The system spends most of its time paging
why: With too little memory for the working sets, processes keep swapping pages in and out instead of working.

q: With 3 frames and FIFO replacement, how many page faults does the string 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2 cause?
why: 1, 2, 3 fault; 4 replaces 1; then 1 replaces 2 and 2 replaces 3. Every reference faults: 6.

q: A semaphore whose value can only be 0 or 1 is called a:
why: A binary semaphore works like a lock for one resource.

q: Virtual memory lets a program:
options: Use more memory than the RAM installed
why: Pages not in use stay on disk, so a program's address space can exceed physical RAM.

q: Belady's anomaly can happen with which page replacement policy?
why: With FIFO, giving more frames can sometimes cause more page faults.

q: What does SQL stand for?
why: SQL is the Structured Query Language.

q: A primary key column can contain:
why: A primary key identifies each row, so it must be unique and never NULL.

q: Which normal form removes transitive dependency?
why: 3NF forbids non-key columns depending on other non-key columns.

q: In ACID, what does the A stand for?
why: Atomicity: a transaction happens completely or not at all.

q: A foreign key is used to:
options: Link rows of one table to another
why: It references the primary key of another table, keeping the link valid.

q: Which isolation problem is a 'dirty read'?
options: Reading data another transaction has not committed
Reading the same row twice and getting different values
New rows appearing in a repeated query
why: A dirty read sees uncommitted changes that may later be rolled back.

q: An index on a column mainly makes which faster?
why: An index is a sorted lookup structure for that column; inserts get a little slower.

q: In an ER diagram, a diamond shape stands for:
why: Rectangles are entities, ovals attributes and diamonds relationships.

q: Which clause filters rows before grouping?
why: WHERE filters rows; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY.

q: Which query counts the rows in a table named students?
why: COUNT(*) counts all rows.

q: Which join returns all rows of the left table even when there is no match on the right?
why: A LEFT JOIN keeps every left row and fills missing right columns with NULL.

q: Which command removes all rows but keeps the table?
why: TRUNCATE empties the table; DROP removes the table itself.

q: Which query finds the second-highest salary from employees(salary)?
options: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);
SELECT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary LIMIT 2;
why: The highest salary below the overall maximum is the second highest.

q: What does SELECT DISTINCT city FROM users; return?
why: DISTINCT removes duplicate values from the result.

q: How many layers does the OSI model have?
why: Physical, data link, network, transport, session, presentation and application.

q: TCP differs from UDP because TCP is:
why: TCP sets up a connection, numbers bytes and resends lost data; UDP does none of that.

q: Which device works at the network layer and forwards packets between networks?
why: Routers use IP addresses to forward packets between networks.

q: The default port for HTTPS is:
why: HTTP uses 80 and HTTPS uses 443.

q: How many usable host addresses does a /26 IPv4 subnet have?
why: A /26 leaves 6 host bits: 2⁶ = 64 addresses, minus the network and broadcast addresses = 62.

q: Which protocol finds the MAC address for a known IP address on a local network?
why: ARP broadcasts 'who has this IP?' and the owner replies with its MAC address.

q: Which of these is a private IPv4 address?
why: 192.168.0.0/16 is one of the private ranges, along with 10.0.0.0/8 and 172.16.0.0/12.

q: The 'ping' command uses which protocol?
why: Ping sends ICMP echo requests and waits for echo replies.

q: Wrapping data and the methods that use it into one unit is called:
why: Encapsulation bundles data with its methods and hides the details.

q: Method overriding is an example of:
why: The method that runs is chosen at run time from the object's actual class.

q: Two methods with the same name but different parameters in one class is:
why: Overloading picks the method by its parameter list at compile time.

q: An abstract class:
why: An abstract class is meant to be extended; you create objects of its subclasses.

q: Java does not allow multiple inheritance of classes mainly to avoid:
why: If two parents had the same method, the child would not know which to inherit. Interfaces avoid this.

q: A constructor:
options: Has the same name as the class and runs when an object is created
why: Constructors set up a new object and have no return type.
